content.text:
**Finding submitted: compliant** (no redline).

**What I checked**

- **Section 9.9 (Audit Procedures)** — the only audit right that binds Sanofi as audited party. It is drafted reciprocally ("each Party shall... permit"), so it also gives us audit rights over RevMed.
- **Section 6.9 (Audit Vendors & Contractors)** — grants *Sanofi* the right to audit RevMed and its subcontractors. This benefits our party, so I did not flag it.
- **Section 9.8 (Records)** — the mutual record-keeping obligation that defines the audit scope.

**Why it meets the preferred position**

| Rule parameter | Section 9.9 |
|---|---|
| Frequency | Capped at [***] per Calendar Year |
| Notice | "at least [***] prior notice" required |
| Independent auditor | "independent auditor of international prominence," reasonably acceptable to the audited Party |
| Confidentiality | Auditor barred from disclosing our Confidential Information; must sign a confidentiality agreement with us |
| Cost | Auditing Party bears full cost unless underpayment exceeds [***]% |
| System access | None — scope limited to books and records under Section 9.8, with a capped look-back and waiver of stale claims |

**Noted, not flagged**

1. The numeric parameters are redacted, so I could not verify them against the 30-day / 5% preferred figures. Worth confirming at unredaction that they land at once per Calendar Year, ≥30 days' notice and a 5% threshold.
2. The frequency cap carries an "unless for cause" exception — a sub-element short of preferred, not a fallback failure.

Both cut the other way too: because the clause is mutual, tightening it would equally shrink our own audit rights over RevMed's royalty and profit/loss-share reporting, so a redline here would be against our interest.
